 Theatrical Releases 
 Here’s everything releasing from November 16 to November 22 in theatres. 
 1. How to Rob a Bank 
 Release Date: November 20 
 Starring Nicholas Hoult, Zoe Kravitz, and more, How to Rob a Bank is a comedy heist film. Although it got an early release in America, the Indian audience is only just getting to watch the film. 
 2. The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping 
 Release Date: November 20 
 Based on the novel by Suzanne Collins, Sunrise on the Reaping stars McKenna Grace, Joseph Zada, Jennifer Lawrence, Ralph Fiennes, Maya Hawke, Jesse Plemons and more. It follows the story of Haymitch Abernathy as he becomes one of the first victors from District 13. 
 3. Om 
 Release Date: November 20 
 Starring Dhanush, Mammootty, Sai Pallavi, and Sreeleela, Om  is an action thriller that follows the underworld exploitation of forests. 
 4. Godzilla Minus Zero 
 Release Date: November 20 
 Directed by Takashi Yamazaki, Godzilla Minus Zero is finally coming to India after the preceding film took over the world with its grandiose display of kaiju. 
 OTT Releases 
 Here’s everything releasing on streaming services between November 16 and November 22. 
 1. Guarding Stars 
 Release Date: November 18 
 Platform: Netflix 
 Starring Leighton Meester and Jared Padalecki, Guarding Stars is a classic rom-com about a no-nonsense bodyguard who protects celebrities and a nonchalant star who charms his way into her heart. 
 2. Madden 
 Release Date: November 18 
 Platform: Amazon Prime Video 
 Directed by David O. Russell, Madden is a biopic of John Madden, starring Nicolas Cage, Christian Bale, Kathryn Hahn, Sienna Miller and more. 
 3. Dhindora S2 
 Release Date: November 20 
 Platform: Netflix 
 Bhuvan Bam is bringing the iconic characters like Titu Mama and more from BB Ki Vines to a bigger platform with the same comedic flair. 
 4. Campus Diaries Season 2 
 Release Date: November 18 
 Platform: MX Player 
 The coming-of-age series is returning with the same flair in exploring the drama and lives of students in universities as they come to deal with life as they enter adulthood.
